relations.note: Ahura Mazda grants or establishes Haurvatat as a divine power.
Haurvatat and Amərətāt form an inseparable pair governing water, plants, drink, food, completeness, and immortality.

relations.myth: Divine gifts obtained through good thought
relations.note: Vohu Manah and Haurvatat appear together within Ahura Mazda’s divine complex.

relations.myth: Wholeness granted through Truth and Order
relations.note: Haurvatat is granted within or through Aša and later joins it in heptadic invocations.
Xšaθra appears with Haurvatat in Gathic petitions and later heptadic lists.
Spandarmad, Hordād, and Amurdād form the feminine triad seated on Ohrmazd’s left.
Ahura Mazda grants Haurvatat and Amərətāt through Spəṇta Mainyu.
Taurwič is Haurvatat’s assigned demonic antagonist and is neutralized or destroyed at renovation.

relations.myth: Demonic assault on water and vegetation
relations.note: Zairika opposes Amərətāt alongside Taurwič, confronting the paired Haurvatat–Amərətāt order.
Angra Mainyu leads the hostile creation opposing Haurvatat’s heptad, though no individual duel is attested.
Hordād and Amurdād, represented by water and plants, oppose Āz’s consuming appetite.
Tīštrya assists Hordād in the cosmic economy of rain and waters.
Wāy is named as Hordād’s cooperating yazata in sustaining the watery creation.
The collective Fravašis assist Hordād in the cosmic ordering of waters.
Some classifications count the holy formula among Hordād’s helpers, though the assignment varies.

relations.myth: Release from pollution and hostile beings
relations.note: Rashnu follows Haurvatat’s invocation and joins male yazatas in freeing the worshipper from pollution.

relations.myth: Liturgical protection with the Amesha Spentas
relations.note: Sraosha appears with Haurvatat’s divine group in protective liturgy; no separate episode survives.
Haurvatat protects or embodies the perfected condition of the divine collective Waters.
Hōm joins Haurvatat’s water-and-immortality complex at renovation without a personal meeting.
Invocation of Haurvatat’s name destroys or repels Nasu and related contaminating beings.
Calling upon Haurvatat’s name is said to destroy or repel innumerable daevas.

relations.myth: Iranian names recontextualized as Qurʾānic angels
relations.note: Hārūt probably preserves Haurvatat’s name, but his Islamic role and mythology are substantially different.
